commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that the corresponding root of y = f(x + 3) is at x = 3, three units to the right.

fixIt.corrected: Inside the brackets means shift LEFT: f(x + 3) is zero where x = -3, to the left of the original root, so the whole graph sits 3 units further left.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: state where the corresponding root of y = f(x + 3) lies, showing in your working why the plus sign moves it left.

commonErrors.misconception: f(x + 3) shifts the graph 3 units to the right.

commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner picks 'It is y = f(x) shifted 3 units to the right' as the statement about the graph of y = f(x + 3).

fixIt.corrected: It is y = f(x) shifted 3 units to the left, because f(x + 3) is zero where x = -3, to the left of the original root.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: explain in one sentence why shifted 3 units to the right is not the correct statement about y = f(x + 3).

commonErrors.misconception: f(x + 3) shifts the graph 3 units to the right.

modelAnswers.answer: f(2x + 6) = f(2(x + 3)): a translation of 3 units to the left, then a horizontal squeeze by a factor of 2.
modelAnswers.question: Rewrite f(2x + 6) in the form f(2(x + c)) and state the horizontal translation it shows.

modelAnswers.answer: A vertical stretch by a factor of 2, followed by a translation of 1 unit up.
modelAnswers.question: Describe fully the transformation that maps y = f(x) onto y = 2f(x) + 1.

nextSteps: Reteach the +c trap from the paired notes trap before any further functions and graphs work: inside the brackets means shift LEFT: f(x + 3) is zero where x = -3, to the left of the original.
Practise factoring out b first whenever a shift inside the brackets is to be read, before stating the translation.
strengths: Most of the class can rewrite an inside change in factored form, such as f(2x + 6) = f(2(x + 3)) on the worksheet.
The class can describe a transformation outside f, such as a vertical stretch by a factor of 2 on the exit ticket.
